title: EU-China trade talks + Academic espionage + Gender gap
gist: Germany and Spain are moving toward backing a Franco-German proposal for a powerful EU anti-distortion trade instrument (including last-resort single-market access restrictions) as China's EU goods surplus rose 13% y/y to EUR 36.5bn in July 2026, setting up sharper EU-China tensions into 2027. The brief also covers tit-for-tat anti-dumping probes, European crackdowns on research ties with China after an MI5 espionage alert, and the tension between China's pro-natalist push and women's economic participation.

insights.claim: Germany and Spain, previously holdouts, have signaled they could back stronger EU trade measures against Chinese state subsidies and industrial overcapacity.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Removal of the key blocking states raises the probability that the EU adopts materially tougher trade tools against Chinese exports.
insights.quote: The EU and China are edging towards a trade confrontation as holdouts Germany and Spain signaled they could back stronger trade measures over Chinese state subsidies and industrial overcapacity

insights.claim: Macron and Merz on October 5, 2026 proposed to Ursula von der Leyen an EU instrument for 'decisive and systemic reaction' against countries that distort competition, including a last-resort restriction on single-market access that could only be blocked by a qualified majority.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A reverse-QMV market-access weapon would be a step-change in EU leverage over Chinese exporters and EU-exposed Chinese firms.
insights.quote: a powerful instrument that allows for decisive and systemic reaction
insights.locator: French President Emmanuel Macron and German Chancellor

insights.claim: China's goods-trade surplus with the EU rose 13% year on year to EUR 36.5 billion in July 2026, driven partly by a near doubling of its surplus with Germany.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A rapidly widening surplus with Germany explains Berlin's political shift and raises pressure on German industrial competitiveness.
insights.quote: its goods-trade surplus with the EU had risen 13 percent year on year to 36.5 billion EUR in July 2026, driven in part by a near doubling of its surplus with Germany
insights.locator: These shifts in Berlin and Madrid

insights.claim: China's Commerce Minister Wang Wentao has reportedly been willing to explore purchase agreements for European goods, but MERICS argues this would not address the EU's core concerns and echoes the Trump-era Phase One deal whose purchase commitments Beijing missed.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Investors should discount any headline purchase-commitment deal as a durable resolution of EU-China trade friction.

insights.claim: MERICS frames the EU-China standoff as mutual dependence: China needs EU demand to absorb overcapacity while the EU cannot afford China-induced de-industrialization, making compromise unlikely.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Structural deadlock implies trade-defense escalation is the base case rather than a negotiated settlement.
insights.quote: China needs EU demand to absorb overcapacity, while the EU can’t afford China-induced de-industrialization.
insights.locator: The EU and China both face substantial risks

insights.claim: If EU leaders back the new trade measures at their October 2026 summit, proposals may take shape by December, setting up sharper tensions with China in 2027.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Provides a concrete timeline for policy risk on China-exposed European exporters and Chinese exporters to Europe.
insights.quote: If EU leaders back the new measures in October, proposals may take shape by December, setting up sharper tensions with China in 2027.
insights.locator: The EU and China both face substantial risks

insights.claim: Spanish Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez called for common EU minimum standards for relations with major economic powers like China even as his government continues to push for more Chinese investment.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Even China-friendly member states are hedging, narrowing Beijing's ability to split the EU.
insights.locator: Five days earlier, Spanish Prime Minister

insights.claim: China's Ministry of Commerce opened an anti-dumping investigation into EU imports of p-nitrotoluene on October 3, 2026, citing recent EU chemical probes as evidence of a campaign against China's chemicals industry.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chemicals is emerging as a front line of EU-China trade retaliation, exposing European specialty chemical exporters.

insights.claim: The EU initiated anti-dumping probes in September 2026 into Chinese imports of cellulose ether, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin).
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Potential duties could support European producers of these chemicals and raise input costs for downstream users.
insights.quote: The EU initiated probes in September into cellulose ether, polyvinyl chloride (PVC) and acetylsalicylic acid (aspirin) imports from China.

insights.claim: MERICS expects European leaders pursuing trade rebalancing with China to face continued Chinese retaliation and persistent tensions.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Each new EU trade-defense action should be expected to trigger a sector-targeted Chinese countermeasure.
insights.quote: leaders should expect continued retaliation from China and persistent tensions
insights.locator: The EU and China are eyeing each other

insights.claim: As the US closed its market to Chinese goods, China's exports to the EU grew 17% in the first half of 2026 to levels unseen since 2022, while exports to ASEAN and Africa grew 26% each and to Latin America 13%.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Trade diversion from US tariffs is flooding third markets, fuelling protectionist reactions globally.
insights.quote: Exports to the EU grew 17 percent in the first half of 2026 and reached levels unseen since 2022.

insights.claim: Intermediate goods now account for around two-thirds of China-ASEAN bilateral trade, reflecting deeper regional production networks, whereas Latin American markets mainly absorb Chinese machinery, electronics and vehicles for domestic use and Mexico imports components for onward export to the US.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Mexico and ASEAN act as transshipment/assembly conduits, making them targets for US rules-of-origin enforcement.
insights.quote: bilateral trade in intermediate goods now accounting for around two-thirds of China–ASEAN trade

insights.claim: MI5 warned UK academic institutions that funding from the China General Technology Research Institute (CGTRI) could support research improving the Chinese Ministry of State Security's espionage capability, affecting more than 100 UK-linked academics, some possibly unaware.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Tighter research-security regimes could curtail AI and cybersecurity collaboration with China and raise compliance costs for universities.
insights.quote: research that directly improves the Chinese Ministry of State Security (MSS)’s technical capability for espionage.

insights.claim: German Research Minister Dorothee Bär told parliament that the rules at the CISPA Helmholtz Center for Information Security were not suitable for preventing research ending up in the wrong hands, including via insufficiently vetted Chinese partners.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Germany joining the UK signals a Europe-wide shift away from open tech research cooperation with China.

insights.claim: Between 2017 and 2022, UK-based researchers co-authored 17,266 AI papers with Chinese partners while German-based researchers co-wrote about 4,400, per MERICS research.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The scale of UK-China AI co-authorship shows how much collaboration is at risk from decoupling of research ties.
insights.quote: UK-based researchers between 2017 and 2022 co-authored 17,266 AI papers with Chinese partners, while German-based ones jointly wrote about 4,400
insights.locator: The disclosures by Germany and the UK

insights.claim: MERICS predicts that even longstanding, uncontroversial-looking academic partnerships with China will face tougher questions from European governments.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Expect broader due-diligence requirements spilling over into corporate R&D partnerships.
insights.quote: Even longstanding academic partnerships that look uncontroversial are likely to face tougher questions
insights.locator: European governments are tightening their scrutiny

insights.claim: China re-entered the top 100 of the World Economic Forum's gender-gap ranking, outperforming South Korea, Japan and India, with its 'economic participation and opportunity' score about 10 percentage points higher than in 2006.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Rising female formal-economy participation supports China's labor supply as the population ages.
insights.locator: China inches up in gender-gap ranking

insights.claim: In China 76% of mothers are mainly responsible for children's everyday care and women spend almost twice as much time as men on unpaid work, according to a national survey and an ILO report.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Unequal care burdens are a structural headwind to Beijing's attempts to lift birth rates.
insights.locator: China inches up in gender-gap ranking

insights.claim: MERICS argues that if women continue to bear most of the cost of childbearing and caregiving, Beijing's push to raise marriage and birth rates could stymie further gains in women's economic participation.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Pro-natalist policy without care support could reduce female labor force participation, weighing on growth potential.
insights.quote: if women continue to bear most of the cost of childbearing and caregiving, efforts to raise marriage and birth rates could stymie further gains in women’s economic participation.

insights.claim: Chinese localities had processed over 920,000 marriage registrations under 'nationwide portability' rules by the end of August 2026, part of efforts to make marriage easier.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Administrative easing of marriage is one lever of Beijing's demographic policy that may support wedding-related consumption.

insights.claim: China recorded a single-day record of 25,204,000 domestic train trips on October 1, 2026, aided by a holiday calendar that let workers take 13 consecutive days off using only three days of annual leave.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Record travel volumes point to resilient services and travel demand in China despite weak goods consumption narratives.

insights.claim: Volkswagen's PowerCo and Gotion High-tech have initiated agreements to set up three battery joint ventures in Spain, Slovakia and Morocco while the EU considers tougher foreign investment requirements in strategic sectors including batteries.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Chinese battery makers are localizing in Europe, but face regulatory risk from incoming EU investment screening.

insights.claim: JD.com expects EU approval for its USD 2.5 billion bid for German electronics retailer Ceconomy, though the European Commission is investigating whether Beijing granted it financial advantages.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: The deal is a test case for the EU Foreign Subsidies Regulation applied to Chinese acquisitions.

insights.claim: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek is reportedly set to raise more than CNY 80 billion (USD 11.9 billion) in a funding round that could reach CNY 100 billion, expected to close in October 2026.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: A round of this size signals deep capital availability for Chinese frontier AI and intensifying competition with US labs.

insights.claim: Huawei and Qualcomm signed a multi-year patent cross-licensing agreement covering 5G, computing, AI and networking, with Qualcomm also purchasing certain Huawei-held US patents.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: Resolves IP friction and creates a licensing revenue stream for Huawei despite US restrictions.

insights.claim: China has proposed Song Li as a late candidate for WHO leadership, seeking to exploit US funding withdrawal and Trump's criticism of the organization to gain influence.
insights.speaker: MERICS
insights.so_what: US retreat from multilateral bodies opens institutional space for Chinese influence.
